newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia vehicle sales fall 10.6 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Colombia vehicle sales fall 10.6 pct in 1996.

text.p: Sales of new vehicles fell 10.6 percent in Colombia in 1996 compared to 1995, Colombia-based vehicle assemblers said in a news release Friday.
They said sales of private and commercial vehicles last year totalled 117,635 against 131,624 in 1995.
General Motor's Chevrolet notched up the biggest share of sales, through local assembler General Motors-Colmotores. It sold 38,577 vehicles, or 32.8 percent of total sales.

Second were sales of Mazda vehicles, through local assembler Compania Colombiana Automotriz, with 17.7 percent of the market, or 20,825 sales. Renault sales accounted for 17.2 percent of the market with 20,250 sales. Renault vehicles are assembled in Colombia by Sofasa.
Imported vehicles of other makes made up 32.3 percent of total sales.
The year-end figure was made up of 74,328 private vehicles and 43,307 commercial vehicles.
